newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to set April basic interest rate today.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to set April basic interest rate today.

text.p: The Monetary Policy Committee was expected on Wednesday to set Brazil's basic monthly interest rate (TBC) at between 1.58 percent and 1.60 percent for April, down from 1.62 percent in March, economists and traders said.

"The market had been expecting a four-basis point cut until the higher-than-expected mini-band depreciation this week. Now it looks like there's a 50-50 chance of a two- or four-basis point cut," said Marcelo Carvalho, chief economist for J.P. Morgan in Brazil.
The Monetary Policy Committee has cut the TBC by four basis points every month since October.

But the Central Bank's decision to lower the foreign exchange rate mini-band this week by 0.28 percent against the dollar -- compared to the standard 0.10-0.15 percent decline -- has caused some in the market to expect a smaller interest rate cut to offset the steeper exchange rate depreciation.
"We're looking for something between two and four basis points, but we wouldn't be surprised if they decided to leave it unchanged," said one forex trader.
Over the next few months, the monetary committee is expected to slow rate cuts to about two basis points a month and then leave rates alone.
A Reuter survey of eight banks and brokerage houses in Brazil forecasts the committee will cut rates until monthly interest rates reach 1.45 percent.
